articles.title: Vinay Prasad Unloads: 'Fauci Was Wrong About Almost Every Single Pandemic Policy He Advanced'
articles.summary: Former FDA insider and epidemiologist Vinay Prasad delivers a scathing indictment of Anthony Fauci, stating plainly that nearly every major pandemic policy Fauci championed was wrong. Prasad also takes aim at the structural rot inside public health institutions and weighs in on RFK Jr.'s efforts to dismantle pharma capture at HHS. This is the kind of accountability interview the mainstream media refuses to air.

articles.title: Blood Clots, Vaccines, and the Institutional Silence That's Killing People

Dr. Joseph Varon argues that common-sense clinical signals were deliberately ignored by health authorities protecting a preferred narrative. The piece names the systemic failure that has allowed preventable deaths to be waved away as coincidence.

articles.title: Doctors Are Being Forced Out for Telling the Truth: UK GP Investigated as 'Transphobic' After Raising Safety Concerns

The tribunal process was weaponized not to protect patients but to silence dissent. This is medical censorship with a new ideological veneer.

articles.title: Perioperative Vaccination: The Medical Establishment Is Running Experiments on Surgical Patients Without Calling It That
articles.summary: Dr. Clayton J. Baker at Brownstone Institute exposes the push to vaccinate patients in the perioperative window — immediately before or after surgery — a practice with no rigorous safety evidence and profound ethical violations. Administering immunologically active agents to anesthetized or post-surgical patients without meaningful informed consent is not medicine; it is coercion dressed in a white coat. The medical literature supporting this practice is thin, the conflicts of interest are thick.

articles.title: How Political Meddling Destroyed American Medicine — And the Institutions That Were Supposed to Protect It

The piece documents how hospitals, the FDA, CDC, and NIH functioned as enforcement arms of a political agenda rather than scientific bodies. Trust has not recovered — because the institutions have not changed.

articles.title: Texas Forces Children's Hospital to Open Detransition Clinic After $10M Settlement — The Medical Establishment Fought This Every Step of the Way
articles.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton's landmark settlement with Texas Children's Hospital has resulted in the opening of the first detransition clinic in the state, a direct rebuke of a hospital system that was performing gender interventions on minors. The $10 million penalty and mandated clinic represent the first time a major U.S. pediatric institution has been held legally accountable for gender medicine harms. Detransitioners who were failed by the system are now speaking out.

articles.title: Vitamin D Research the Mainstream Won't Touch: International Forum Presents Data Agencies Have Ignored for Years

The RDA remains criminally low while the data screams otherwise.

articles.title: CDC Caught in Deliberate Cover-Up of Vaccine Injury Data, Brownstone Investigation Finds

This is not incompetence — Tucker argues it was a coordinated institutional decision to protect the vaccine program over patient safety.

articles.title: Doctors Forced to Vaccinate Surgical Patients Perioperatively — The Ethics Atrocity No One Is Talking About
articles.summary: Clayton J. Baker, MD details the coercive practice of administering COVID vaccines to patients immediately before or after surgery — a window when immune systems are stressed and informed consent is functionally impossible. Baker argues this protocol violated foundational medical ethics and was pushed through hospital systems without independent safety review. The piece names the institutional pressure that silenced physicians who objected.

articles.title: Big Pharma's Hostages: How Federal Policy Traps Patients in a Captured Drug System

The piece challenges Trump-era HHS to follow through on reform rhetoric rather than repeating the pattern of regulatory capture that has defined decades of drug policy. A damning first-person account of what systemic pharma corruption looks like from the inside.

This is nutrition science suppression with measurable mortality consequences.

articles.title: ENO2 and Tumor Glycolysis: Metabolic Cancer Research the Oncology Establishment Won't Fund
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS ONE implicates ENO2-driven glycolysis — a metabolic pathway, not a genetic mutation — as a key driver of hepatocellular carcinoma progression and a potential prognostic marker. This work advances the metabolic theory of cancer, first articulated by Otto Warburg, that tumors exploit fermentation-based energy production rather than oxidative phosphorylation. The oncology establishment has spent decades marginalizing metabolic approaches in favor of targeted genetic therapies that cost hundreds of thousands of dollars per patient.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces FTC Fraud Complaint and Securities Lawsuit — The Telehealth Gold Rush Has a Dirty Secret

This is the collision of Silicon Valley's 'disruptive health' branding with the same deceptive marketing tactics that characterize legacy pharma — just faster, cheaper, and with better Instagram ads. Investors and patients are both the marks.

articles.title: Smoking Gun: NIH Scientist Proposed Engineering Furin Cleavage Site Into Coronavirus Weeks Before Pandemic
articles.summary: Newly surfaced emails show NIH virologist Vincent Munster proposed engineering a furin cleavage site into a coronavirus spike protein on October 6, 2019 — weeks before the pandemic began — to 'enhance infectivity.' This modification is the exact genetic feature at the center of the lab-leak debate, and it directly implicates NIH-funded research in the architecture of SARS-CoV-2. The emails contradict years of official denial and raise unresolved questions about whether NIH-linked scientists had foreknowledge of or involvement in engineering the pandemic pathogen.

The piece names the mechanisms: agency capture, media coordination, and financial conflicts of interest that turned health institutions into enforcement arms of pharmaceutical policy. What was once called paranoia is now documented institutional failure.

articles.title: Vitamin D Science Has Been Systematically Undervalued — International Forum Pushes Back
articles.summary: The 2024 International Virtual Vitamin D Forum aggregated research demonstrating vitamin D's broad immune, skeletal, and metabolic roles that far exceed the minimal standards set by government dietary guidelines. Decades of research linking vitamin D deficiency to cancer, autoimmune disease, and respiratory infection vulnerability have been sidelined in favor of pharmaceutical interventions that cost far more and carry greater risk. The suppression of low-cost nutritional interventions in favor of patentable drugs remains one of the most consequential conflicts of interest in modern medicine.

articles.title: Plant Compound Curcumin Selectively Kills Cancer Cells — Unprofitable, So It Stays in the Lab
articles.summary: Researchers at Wroclaw Medical University found that curcumin — a non-patentable plant compound — demonstrated selective anticancer activity against fibrosarcoma cells while sparing healthy muscle tissue, outperforming or matching several other natural compounds tested. This kind of research consistently fails to attract NIH funding or clinical trial investment because there is no patent value and therefore no return for pharmaceutical sponsors. The data accumulates in journals; the oncology establishment ignores it.

articles.title: Texas Forces Children's Hospital to Open Detransition Clinic After $10M Settlement — The Medical Establishment Called This Impossible
articles.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secured a landmark $10 million settlement with Texas Children's Hospital that included a legally mandated requirement to open the state's first detransition clinic — providing care for patients harmed by gender transition interventions. For years, mainstream medicine denied that detransition was a significant phenomenon and marginalized clinicians who documented harm. This settlement forces institutional medicine to confront the patients it created and then abandoned.

articles.title: COVID Surveillance Systematically Undercounted Cases in Poor Minority Neighborhoods — The Data Was Always Biased
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed PLOS ONE study of Miami-Dade County reveals that passive COVID-19 surveillance systems structurally undercounted infection burden in low-income and minority communities, while affluent neighborhoods with greater healthcare access dominated reported case counts. This matters because the skewed data shaped policy, resource allocation, and the public narrative about who COVID was actually hitting hardest. Epidemiological decisions made on corrupted surveillance data produced inequitable and scientifically invalid public health responses.
